Description: Defines a class: the container where all Java code lives
Access modifier: lets other classes and the robot's system use the class or method
Inheritance: the child class gets everything the parent class already has
Brings in a class from a library (like the FTC SDK) so you can use it in the file
Braces: mark where a class or method starts and ends; they always come in pairs
Ends every statement; lines that open a brace { don't take one
Naming convention for classes: every word starts with a capital letter
A public class must have the same name as its .java file, capital letters included
Metadata that describes the code to the compiler or the system; it doesn't run anything
Says you're replacing a method from the parent class; the compiler flags it if the name is misspelled
Registers the OpMode as a driver-controlled program so it shows up on the Driver Station
Hides the OpMode from the Driver Station menu without deleting it (handy for tests)
Return type: the method does its job but gives no value back
Sends a value back from a method that isn't void and ends it
Runs once when INIT is pressed; used to get the robot ready
Repeats about 50 times per second while the OpMode is running
Sends a label and a value to the Driver Station screen for debugging
Compares the text of two Strings; == only checks whether they are the same object
Single-line comment: the compiler ignores everything after it on that line
Block comment: ignores everything between /* and */, even across several lines
Example: /* Espera 500 ms a que el sensor se estabilice */

Description: Javadoc: a block comment that tools read to generate documentation and hover tooltips
Example: /** Se ejecuta una vez al presionar INIT. */

Description: Java tells upper and lower case apart: potencia and Potencia are different names; keywords are always lowercase
Example: int potencia = 1; // Potencia would fail: it doesn't exist

Description: Java ignores spaces, tabs and line breaks; blocks are marked by braces, not indentation
Every opening parenthesis needs a closing one; if one is missing, the program won't compile
Registers the OpMode in the Driver Station's Autonomous list instead of TeleOp
A named spot in memory that holds a value; its size depends on its type
Naming convention for variables: start lowercase, every next word starts with a capital
type name; reserves the space with a type and a name; required before using the variable
Stores the value on the right in the variable on the left; it doesn't mean equality
A variable can get new values many times; it always keeps the latest and the old one is lost
type name = value; declares and assigns in one line; the most common way
Class fields with no value start at 0 (numbers) or false (boolean); a local variable must be assigned before it is read
Example: public class Robot { int vueltas; boolean listo; }

Description: Java's 8 built-in types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean; FTC mostly uses int, double and boolean
Example: int a = 1; double b = 0.5; boolean c = true;

Description: 8-bit whole number: from -128 to 127
16-bit whole number (-32,768 to 32,767); almost never used in FTC
A single Unicode character, in single quotes
32-bit whole number (-2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647); the standard for counting
64-bit whole number (up to ~9 quintillion); use it when an int isn't big enough
32-bit decimal (~7 digits of precision); smaller than a double
64-bit decimal (~15-17 digits); Java's default decimal type and what sensors return
Holds only true or false; it doesn't accept 1 or 0 and can't be added
Java's logical values; always lowercase (True won't compile)
Class for holding text; written with a capital S and the value goes in double quotes
Wrap a text (String); single quotes ' ' are only for a char
Primitives (int, double) are lowercase; String is a class, so it starts with a capital letter
Joins texts, or text with numbers, into one String; it doesn't add spaces on its own
Where a variable exists: it's born at its declaration and dies at the } of the block where it was created
Example: int x = 5; { int y = 4; x = x + y; } // aquí y ya no existe

Description: Any section of code between { and }; each block has its own scope
Variables from an outer block are visible in inner blocks, but not the other way around
